correctness.rationale: For connected finite simple G and three protected terminals, each of m=n-3 other sites survives independently with probability p and one nonedge may be added. The gain from edge e is ∑_{k=0}^m c_e(k) p^k(1-p)^{m-k}, c_e(k) counting survivor subsets where e bridges exactly two terminal-containing components; this criterion is both necessary and sufficient. A complete published unlabelled atlas of 1253 graphs through n=7 (including 32191 connected rooted nontrivial triple-terminal cases) has for each a coefficientwise dominating available edge, proving p-uniform optimality conditional on atlas completeness. Independent networkx.graph_atlas_g exhaustive loop repeated all 32191 instances with 16+190+2200+29785 by order, each passing. The explicit connected eight-vertex nine-edge witness has 19 nonedges; gain A=(0,1,4,3,0,0), gain B=(0,2,5,2,0,0), all 17 others dominated by at least one. Difference p(1-p)^2(p^2+p-1) switches unique winner at golden-ratio conjugate. All subsets recomputed independently; no unbounded graph theorem claimed.

value.rationale: The first network size allowing an edge-augmentation optimum to depend on habitat survival probability is a natural sharp finite cutoff with practical interpretation for robust corridor planning.
